message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and reviewed the live quote, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 for a total of $9,801.00. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 **total net sales of $391.035 billion** (up 2% year over year from $383.285 billion), driven by Services growth of 13% to $96.169 billion and a total gross margin of 46.2% (up from 44.1%), with operating income of $123.216 billion and operating cash flow of $118.254 billion. Net income of $93.736 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were down year over year, but only because of a one-time $10.2 billion net income tax charge tied to the European Commission State Aid Decision — a non-operating event, since operating income and cash generation both improved. The order was sized to the mandate: 44 shares at ~$222.75 kept the notional at $9,801, under both the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap (this was the only trade today), the limit sat essentially at the current ask of $222.72 (~0.01% above market), it was a buy in an authorized name, and no funds were moved out of the account.
